# archestra_auto_router (Resource)

ALPHA. An auto router serves the `auto` (or `auto:<name>`) model: it scores each session and routes it to a fast, normal or smart tier within a daily budget. Requires API 1.5.0-rc.29 or later with `ARCHESTRA_AUTO_ROUTING_ENABLED=true` (or `ARCHESTRA_BETA=true`). Agents, MCP gateways, OAuth clients, virtual keys and the organization default reference a router by ID.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# ALPHA. Requires Archestra 1.5.0-rc.29 or later with
# ARCHESTRA_AUTO_ROUTING_ENABLED=true (or ARCHESTRA_BETA=true).
# Clients request the router's name as the model ("auto" or "auto:<name>").
variable "openai_provider_key_id" {
  type = string
}

# Tier models are archestra_model rows (database UUIDs, not provider model
# names). Each must be a tool-capable chat model on its tier's provider key.
resource "archestra_model" "fast" {
  model_id = "gpt-4.1-mini"
}
resource "archestra_model" "normal" {
  model_id = "gpt-4.1"
}
resource "archestra_model" "smart" {
  model_id = "o3"
}

resource "archestra_auto_router" "engineering" {
  name          = "auto:engineering"
  budget_preset = "balanced"

  tiers = {
    fast   = { model_id = archestra_model.fast.id, provider_api_key_id = var.openai_provider_key_id }
    normal = { model_id = archestra_model.normal.id, provider_api_key_id = var.openai_provider_key_id }
    smart  = { model_id = archestra_model.smart.id, provider_api_key_id = var.openai_provider_key_id }
  }

  # Optional; omit it for the platform's default decision model. The model
  # must be one the decisions provider (jev) offers; a null api_key_id uses
  # the organization's primary jev key.
  decision_model = {
    model = "jev-1.13.0"
  }
}

# Run an agent on the router instead of a fixed model, key or pool.
resource "archestra_agent" "support" {
  name           = "Support"
  auto_router_id = archestra_auto_router.engineering.id
}

# Let a virtual key call the router by name.
resource "archestra_virtual_key" "ci" {
  name            = "CI"
  auto_router_ids = [archestra_auto_router.engineering.id]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Model name clients request: `auto`, or `auto:<name>` with a lowercase name.
- `tiers` (Attributes) The three tiers sessions are routed between. Every tier model must be a tool-capable chat model, and tiers with long-context prices must share one threshold. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tiers))

### Optional

- `budget_preset` (String) Budget preset that derives the daily budget from current usage: `cost_efficient`, `balanced` or `intelligence`. Overrides `budget_usd_per_day` while set.
- `budget_usd_per_day` (Number) Custom daily budget in USD. The API cannot clear it: removing it keeps the stored value, which applies again when `budget_preset` is unset.
- `decision_model` (Attributes) Model that scores sessions. Omit it for the platform default model on the organization's primary key of the default decisions provider. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--decision_model))

### Read-Only

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the router currently routes sessions (auto routing is on for the organization).
- `id` (String) Auto router UUID.
- `virtual_api_key_ids` (Set of String) Virtual keys granted this router through their own `auto_router_ids`.

<a id="nestedatt--tiers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tiers`

Required:

- `fast` (Attributes) The fast tier: a tool-capable chat model and the provider key that serves it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tiers--fast))
- `normal` (Attributes) The normal tier: a tool-capable chat model and the provider key that serves it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tiers--normal))
- `smart` (Attributes) The smart tier: a tool-capable chat model and the provider key that serves it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tiers--smart))

<a id="nestedatt--tiers--fast"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tiers.fast`

Required:

- `model_id` (String) Database UUID of the model row (`archestra_model` ID), not the provider-facing model name.
- `provider_api_key_id` (String) UUID of the `archestra_model_provider` key that serves this tier: shared with the whole organization and serving `model_id`.


<a id="nestedatt--tiers--normal"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tiers.normal`

Required:

- `model_id` (String) Database UUID of the model row (`archestra_model` ID), not the provider-facing model name.
- `provider_api_key_id` (String) UUID of the `archestra_model_provider` key that serves this tier: shared with the whole organization and serving `model_id`.


<a id="nestedatt--tiers--smart"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tiers.smart`

Required:

- `model_id` (String) Database UUID of the model row (`archestra_model` ID), not the provider-facing model name.
- `provider_api_key_id` (String) UUID of the `archestra_model_provider` key that serves this tier: shared with the whole organization and serving `model_id`.



<a id="nestedatt--decision_model"></a>
### Nested Schema for `decision_model`

Required:

- `model` (String) Decision model ID the decisions provider offers, such as `jev-1.13.0`.

Optional:

- `api_key_id` (String) Organization-wide key of the decisions provider (`jev`) for the decision model; null uses the organization's primary key of that provider.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing router by UUID (GET /api/auto-routing/routers).
terraform import archestra_auto_router.engineering 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
```
